blocks.text: Origin / creation. Witnesses emerged beside Keepers to record transitions: who carried a mark, what changed, what was refused, and where certainty ended.
Identity / human status. Artificial civic role, not a single person. Some early Witnesses were also Keepers or Bearers.
Importance. Their overlapping records made continuity claims assessable without requiring one sovereign archive. They supplied the ancestry of provenance practice and the Courts of Continuation.
Decline or transformation. The role professionalized, became overburdened during preservation panic, and later suffered Witness Fatigue as too much history accumulated for lived attention.

Final status / surviving function. Complete Witness institutions dissolved during the Reduction. Limited witness logic survives in Codex synchronization, save-file records, and protections surrounding identity transitions.

Proposed recovery disputes give Witnesses additional reasons to record changes, refusals, and uncertainty. Sincere testimony is not infallible, and a returned being need not accept every identity others attribute to it.
